fields.label: Compatibility Rule
fields.description: Identical: same ABO. Red Cell: patient can receive own group or O (RhD negative patient needs negative). Plasma: reverse rule. Any: no ABO block (warning only).

fields.label: Shelf Life Help
fields.options:
Where the expiry comes from. Expiry = collection time + the shelf life below. These are the international defaults (WHO / AABB / EU guide). Change them only on your medical director's instruction.
ComponentStore atShelf lifeWhy
Whole Blood2 to 6 °C fridge35 days (CPDA-1 bag)Cold slows the cells. After 35 days fewer than 75% of the red cells survive in the patient. CPD bags without adenine: 21 days.
Red Cells (RBC)2 to 6 °C fridge42 days (SAGM additive)The additive solution feeds the cells longer. Without additive: 35 days.
Platelets (PLT)20 to 24 °C on an agitator5 daysPlatelets die in the cold, so they are kept warm and shaken. Warm storage lets bacteria grow, so the life is short. Never put them in the fridge.
Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP)-18 °C or colder1 yearFreezing within 8 hours keeps the clotting factors (V and VIII). After thawing: use within 24 hours, kept at 2 to 6 °C.
Plasma-18 °C or colder1 yearPlasma frozen later than FFP. Fewer clotting factors, same storage.
Read the bag packet: the anticoagulant printed on it (CPDA-1, CPD + SAGM) decides the Whole Blood and Red Cell life.
